label: Faithful origin-tolerance countermodel checked
meaning: With the origin interface restored (varied origins of one rigidly identified individual, origin-determined access, origin plenitude), every premise of ActualEuclidean.inertNecessaryConcrete except Euclidean access at actual holds while its conclusion fails, so the tolerance rival survives Arrival A in this encoding. The countermodel needs two individuals: the individual necessary relative to the witness world plus (b) must be absent from a successor of actual that plus does not see (aMinus), and the varied individual a is contingent. Group 2 records that the surrogate's own three-offset pattern with the varied individual restored at all offsets does not give a countermodel: that individual exists at every successor of actual. Model claims concern these finite interpretations only; whether a world may lack an actual individual (b at aMinus, a at bMinus) is permitted, not required, by the encoded commitments. Two individuals: any countermodel to Arrival A needs two, already forced by its premises (an individual necessary at the witness world and one contingent there); under the if-half, additionally the successor lacking the necessary individual must be cut off by a second individual's far origin. On a one-individual carrier the arrival's premises are unsatisfiable, so it holds there only vacuously. Scope (semantic challenge 2026-11-10): faithful only to the encoded origin-tolerance commitments (rigid identity; Salmon-style access iff shared individuals have near origins, whose if-half is OPEN; near-origin plenitude; one varied individual), with stipulated absences (a from bMinus and bPlus, b from aMinus) and a stipulated temporal profile not tied to origins; model-witnessed for this finite encoding only. Not tested: counterpart, vague or kind-relative tolerance, or recombination/deletion plenitude.
